# glyhub <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="glyhub logo" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-universe version](https://glycoverse.r-universe.dev/glyhub/badges/version)](https://glycoverse.r-universe.dev/glyhub)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/glycoverse/glyhub/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/glycoverse/glyhub/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/glycoverse/glyhub/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/glycoverse/glyhub)
<!-- badges: end -->

glyhub collects glycomics and glycoproteomics data for the Glycoverse ecosystem,
using the [`GlycomicSE`](https://glycoverse.github.io/glyexp/reference/GlycomicSE.html)
and [`GlycoproteomicSE`](https://glycoverse.github.io/glyexp/reference/GlycoproteomicSE.html) containers from
[glyexp](https://github.com/glycoverse/glyexp). The package is experimental.

## Available data

75 datasets from 47 public GlycoPOST projects are available, including released
glycans, glycosaminoglycan disaccharides and site/charge-resolved glycopeptides.
Objects combine source-defined quantitative tables from the same study and glycan
class where measurement definitions are compatible. GPST000602 is explicitly an
annotated-peak subset with spectrum-specific, unaligned feature identities.
Inclusion does not imply recovery of every experiment in its paper.

Each dataset has its own help page describing the biological system, experimental
design, units, source table and limitations. Use `glyhub_catalog()` for the
complete catalog. N/O classes remain separate; source experiments, sample conditions and replicate
labels remain in `colData`. Feature unions use documented author keys or supported
structures, with an explicit source-coverage mask for unmeasured combinations.

**For GlycoPOST datasets, zero-valued abundances are stored as NA in the distributed assays.** Original
values, source-missing values and conflict masks remain in metadata. No imputation
or renormalization is applied. Unknown molecular annotations remain NA without
removing quantitative rows. Structures are encoded only from explicit source
structural evidence. Unresolved bonds and attachment positions remain uncertain.

## Installation

Install the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/glycoverse/glyhub):

```r
if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pak", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
options(repos = c(
  glycoverse = "https://glycoverse.r-universe.dev",
  CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
))
pak::pkg_install("glycoverse/glyhub")
```

The Glycoverse repository provides dependencies such as `glyexp`. `pak` also
resolves required Bioconductor packages for your R version.

## Example

```r
x <- glyhub::glyhub_load("glyhub_GPST000738_N_B4GalT1")
dim(x)
data.frame(as.list(S4Vectors::metadata(x)$processing_counts))
```

All datasets use `glyhub_load()`. `SummarizedExperiment::assay(x)` contains the
curated abundance matrix; `S4Vectors::metadata(x)$raw_abundance` preserves the
unconverted values. `rowData(x)` retains typed glyrepr annotations and source
evidence, and `colData(x)` retains source conditions and observation locations.

## Loading external data

The 83 existing released datasets are stored in the [Glyhub data release](https://github.com/glycoverse/glyhub/releases/tag/data-v0.1.0).
The package includes the catalog and loader code, with no bundled data objects.
Fourteen non-CPTAC datasets are available in the existing
[data release](https://github.com/glycoverse/glyhub/releases/tag/data-v0.1.0).
Eight have explicit PRIDE CC0 source-file licenses. For the human atlas, mouse
brain, lung and two HCC objects, source-license scope remains unresolved;
publication does not establish or grant a new license. See the
[per-object source and publication records](data-raw/noncptac/publication-decisions.tsv).

```{r}
head(glyhub::glyhub_catalog()[, c("dataset", "source", "bytes")])
```

Use either the common loader or a dataset's own function. Both share the same
verified cache and return the same object:

```r
x <- glyhub::glyhub_load("glyhub_CPTAC_CCRCC")
x <- glyhub::glyhub_CPTAC_CCRCC()

x <- glyhub::glyhub_GPST000738_N_B4GalT1()
x <- glyhub::glyhub_load("glyhub_GPST000738_N_B4GalT1", offline = TRUE)

# Original CPTAC source archive; returns a verified local file path.
raw_file <- glyhub::glyhub_CPTAC_CCRCC(kind = "raw")
# Equivalent: glyhub::glyhub_load("glyhub_CPTAC_CCRCC", kind = "raw")
```

**Breaking interface change:** all former dataset objects are now functions.
Add `()` when using a dataset name directly, or pass its name to `glyhub_load()`.
LazyData, variable-style access and `data()` access are no longer provided.
`glyhub_catalog()` lists all curated datasets; `kind = "raw"` lists available
source archives, currently the eight CPTAC archives. Dataset help topics retain
scientific details and source references.

Every resource is checked against its size and SHA-256 before use. For released resources, the first call
requires an internet connection; subsequent calls reuse the cache. Set `cache_dir`
or option `glyhub.cache_dir` to select its location. `refresh = TRUE` retrieves
the pinned version again; `offline = TRUE` prohibits downloads and requires a
valid cached file. Delete cached files to clear the cache.

## Non-CPTAC studies

These datasets prefer deposited reporter intensities, chromatographic peak areas,
or the authors' raw expression matrices. Source zeros are preserved. No additional
normalization, imputation, logarithm, or inverse transformation is applied.

`glyhub_PXD052447_N_Tissues()` contains 205,904 deposited PSM rows across 18 TMT
channels from three tissues of two mice, with technical replication. PSM rows are
not unique glycopeptides. Rows without glycan annotations and unused or unmapped
channels remain explicitly identifiable in the source annotations. Measurement
channels and technical runs are not automatically independent people or animals.

Some studies provide only processed quantitative tables. Their help pages and
metadata state the scale, source normalization, transformations, imputation and
feature selection. In particular, the HCC discovery table contains selected
features, so it is not suitable for unbiased feature discovery or classifier
performance estimation. `metadata(x)$raw_abundance` preserves source numbers;
it does not imply that a processed source table is raw intensity. The earliest
unnormalized HCC clinical matrix was not available through the inspected sources;
the linear QC table represents a different experiment and cannot replace it.

See [the source-selection audit and rebuild instructions](data-raw/noncptac/README.md).
Data licenses remain separate from the package's code license. PRIDE CC0 evidence
applies to the eight DQGlyco/Glyco-DIA objects, not automatically to publisher
supplements or objects with unresolved source-license scope. Original
sources, attribution, processing and limitations remain in each object's metadata
and the [publication records](data-raw/noncptac/publication-decisions.tsv).

`glyhub_MSV000089484_N_HCC()` provides the original 11,001 × 12 pGlycoQuant
cell-line table. By an explicit user-confirmed curation convention, 40,338 source
`-1` values become assay `NA`; an author definition of this code has not been
located. All 2,137 zeros and positive intensities are unchanged. The original
values, including `-1`, remain in `metadata(x)$raw_abundance`. No log transform,
normalization, imputation or row filtering is added. The 6,435-row filtered sheet
is not included as another cohort. Attachment-license scope remains unconfirmed.
